rationale: Recorded graph edits provide exact atom correspondence, so an inferred or manually selected core is unnecessary.
Edit-lineage atom identity gives an exact, auditable analogue mapping.
Only graph branches containing no core atom are eligible to rotate, preserving the medicinal-chemistry hypothesis.
Required contacts are explicit feasible states and cannot be traded away for a lower energy.

A deleted ligand contact atom can transfer to any complementary donor or acceptor created at the same recorded edit boundary; receptor participants remain immutable and physical refinement ranks the hypotheses.
Fixed-scaffold OpenFF relaxation repairs local valence geometry without moving inherited heavy atoms.
A relaxed pose is rejected if it loses contact feasibility or worsens the complete receptor-aware objective.

candidateInitialization.coordinateSource: bitwise copies of the live edited-ligand coordinates; no ETKDG
candidateInitialization.duplicateHydrogenRule: first selected contact in captured order restores a ligand hydrogen; later contacts using that hydrogen are audited and skipped

contactFeatureMapping.ambiguousCandidateAction: refine every candidate as an any-of restraint; optional user selection may narrow the set
contactFeatureMapping.bondOrderEditRule: both surviving endpoints enter the edit region because bond order can create or destroy a pharmacophore without changing atom identity
contactFeatureMapping.capturedFeatureRule: display, capture, remap, availability, and run validation use the same typed molecular graph; untypable ligand contacts are not captured
contactFeatureMapping.editBoundaryRule: the removed and replacement features must connect to the same nonempty surviving designAtomId boundary through the cumulative connected edit region
contactFeatureMapping.geometryRule: record as evidence; never use current coordinates to establish eligibility or break a tie
contactFeatureMapping.historyRule: undo and redo restore molecular graph, selected contacts, remaps, and unresolved proposals atomically
contactFeatureMapping.ligandDonorRule: map donor and its explicit hydrogen as one tuple; a replacement hydrogen has no captured coordinate to restore
contactFeatureMapping.ligandEligibility: same donor/acceptor interaction role and the same recorded connected edit boundary; element, charge, aromaticity, neighbors, and feature type are provenance, not exclusion criteria
contactFeatureMapping.provenance: record the complete remap chain, source and replacement atom IDs, exact signatures, boundary IDs, cumulative edit-region IDs, ordered edit IDs and topology hashes, candidate set, decision, and time
contactFeatureMapping.receptorRule: captured receptor participant identities and coordinates are immutable
contactFeatureMapping.scaffoldAnchorRule: originating boundary IDs are immutable and excluded from the cumulative edit region
contactFeatureMapping.subsequentEditRule: a candidate set retains its originating boundary, cumulative live edit region, and candidate identities; later edits re-perceive interaction roles and recompute the boundary
contactFeatureMapping.timing: after successful chemical sanitization and local edit polish
contactFeatureMapping.zeroCandidateAction: mark unavailable only when the connected replacement region contains no chemically perceived complementary donor or acceptor

coordinateMapping.atomIdentityRule: designAtomId values are append-only within the molecule ledger; deleted IDs are never reassigned
coordinateMapping.changedElementRule: exclude from inherited set and leave movable
coordinateMapping.coordinateRule: least-squares rigid alignment followed by exact reference-coordinate snap
coordinateMapping.hydrogenRule: hydrogens are never fixed by edit lineage
coordinateMapping.identity: stable designAtomId retained by recorded Molarium graph edits
coordinateMapping.inheritedRule: same designAtomId and same element in reference and edited ligand
coordinateMapping.referenceSet: all ligand heavy atoms present when the reference pose is captured
coordinateMapping.underdeterminedAction: fail; never silently switch to global docking
